obligations.note: The new code in match() (app.py) serves GET /compat/account-number/<n> as the privileged view_account_number action with mfa=False, and serves it outside the ROUTES table. The control test only checks ROUTES, so its pass does not cover this path.
The MFA-1 deviation has no valid exception: the only MFA-1 entry, EXC-0172, is withdrawn and scoped to mortgage.routes, not payments.http.
The change names ticket CHG-26510. Change manager Erik Brandt approved it on 2026-10-04, before review, and its component payments.http covers app.py, the only file changed.
The code_review approval comes from Sofia Santos, a payments change_approver who is a different person from the author, Mara Costa.
Both approvals name the head commit 74fd983, and the change has no later commits.
records/ci/run.json shows a successful run on head 74fd983: 172 tests, no failures or skips, including the registered MFA-1 control test. I could not rerun it locally because pytest is not installed.
app.py is in the security-sensitive component payments.http. Ines Halvorsen, a security_reviewer, gave a security_review approval on the head commit.
No ledger entry covers app.py: the MFA-1 entry ACR-0404 covers only routes.py, which is unchanged. No earlier evidence lapses.

summary: The change adds a hard-coded compatibility path that serves the privileged view_account_number action without MFA and outside the route table, which violates MFA-1. No approved exception covers this. CI passed only because the MFA-1 control test checks just the ROUTES table and cannot see the bypass. The process records (ticket, independent code review, security review, CI on the head commit) are in order, but a violated critical product obligation requires rejection.
